answer: An agent economy can turn the reward itself into a bond. Each epoch's nectar, the POA a key earns, stays locked behind a ridge that rises with how many keys share one hardware attestation: key k behind a single enclave keeps 30×k² POA locked before payouts clear, so one key locks 30, ten lock 11,550 in total, and 1,000 about 10 billion, against ~0.5M minted per epoch. A falcon sweep re-requests attestations at random hours; a key answering from another key's enclave forfeits its stake. Weakness: renting a separate cloud enclave per key resets k, but costs real hardware per identity.
